1972.notes: Secondary source (The Portsmouth Times, Associated Press report 'SORTA To Accept Cincinnati Agreement', February 1, 1973, p. 7, via Google News Archive): beginning April 1 [1973] the city earnings tax will be raised .3 per cent to 2 per cent to finance the purchase of Cincinnati Transit, the increase Cincinnatians approved in the November [1972] election. The Youngstown Vindicator's AP report 'Cincinnatians Approve Buying Transit System' (November 8, 1972, p. 18, https://books.google.com/books?id=uxFcAAAAIBAJ&pg=PA18&article_id=1082,3255533) says the November 7, 1972 charter amendment would increase the city earnings tax from 1.7 to 2 per cent. So 1.7% applied throughout 1972 (ACIR: 1.7% at December 31, 1971; 2.0% at July 1, 1973). Two reports of the same AP service.

1974.notes: Cincinnati Municipal Code § 311-1(c)-(d) (Authority to levy tax; effective periods; Municode) states that the general levy of § 311-3(a) applies to income 'earned or received on or after April 1, 1973' and the 0.1% infrastructure levy of § 311-3(b) to income 'earned or received after July 1, 1988'; the city's 2001 financial report describes the 2.1% as 1.55% general + 0.15% permanent improvement + 0.3% transit + 'the latest increase of 0.1% enacted July 1, 1988'. So 2.0% applied from April 1, 1973 until the July 1988 increase, including all of 1974; the ACIR editions print 2.0% at July 1, 1973, July 1, 1976, October 1, 1979 and for 1983-1987. No document for 1974 itself.

1995.notes: The City of Cincinnati 2001 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (financial section p. 37) states: 'The City's income tax of 2.1% is subdivided into four components. The first component is the latest increase of .1% enacted July 1, 1988, to be spent only for the maintenance of the City's infrastructure' (the others being .3% transit, .15% permanent improvement and 1.55% general). So 2.1% applied from July 1, 1988 through 2001; the ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism editions print 2.1% for 1988-1994 and the Department of Taxation's LG-11 table 2.1% for 2000. No document for 1995 itself.
